5	## Purpose
6	
7	Deptrac enforces dependency direction between architectural layers. It should describe the project's real boundaries, not a generic web stack. The same setup should work for web apps, CLI apps, workers, libraries, packages, and modular codebases after adapting layer names and collectors.
8	
9	## Installation
10	
11	Use Composer when the target project can satisfy Deptrac's runtime constraints:
12	
13	```bash
14	composer require --dev deptrac/deptrac
15	```
16	
17	Do not force installation with `--ignore-platform-reqs`. For libraries and developer tools that support older PHP versions, allow Composer to resolve different Deptrac versions per PHP runtime. A normal single `composer.lock` is fine when it works for the supported dependency graph. Use PHP-versioned lock files when old PHP support requires a different graph and supply-chain pinning is required. If the target project supports an older PHP runtime than any compatible Deptrac can run on, run Deptrac from a separate toolchain or PHAR on a newer PHP runtime.
18	
19	Older Deptrac lines used for PHP 8.0 compatibility may not provide `vendor/bin/deptrac`. In that case, use a project-root launcher such as `deptrac.php` that prefers `vendor/bin/deptrac` and falls back to `vendor/deptrac/deptrac/deptrac.php`, then call it from Composer:
20

1	# DocGen Configuration
2	
3	DocGen configuration generated by the `/setup-toolkit-doc-gen` skill.
4	
5	## Purpose
6	
7	DocGen is a first-party CLI that generates a complete static HTML documentation site for the composer packages of a
8	project. AI agents work best when the whole picture of a codebase — interfaces, relationships, architectural layers,
9	and behavioral guarantees — is visible in one place; DocGen renders exactly that, with docs.rs-grade information
10	density, from the code and its PHPDoc without any manual documentation step.
11	
12	## Command
13	
14	```bash
15	vendor/bin/doc-gen --config=doc.yaml
16	```
17	
18	Exit codes:
19	
20	- `0`: documentation generated
21	- `2`: configuration or runtime error
22	
23	The config file is optional: without `doc.yaml`, the project root and `packages/*` are documented into `build/docs`.
24	
25	CLI options override the configuration: `--output=DIR`, `--vendor[=GLOBS]` (document installed runtime dependencies),
26	`--vendor-dev[=GLOBS]` (document installed dev dependencies), `--coverage=DIR` (PHPUnit `--coverage-xml` report),
27	`--base-url=URL` (the address the site is published at),
28	`--diff=RANGE` / `--base=REVISION` / `--head=REVISION` (compare two git revisions),
29	`--serve[=HOST:PORT]` (preview the generated site locally), `--memory-limit=VALUE`, `--jobs=N`,
30	`--cache-dir=DIR`, `--no-cache`, and `--clear-cache`.
31	
32	Documenting a large dependency tree needs more memory than the common 128M default, so the limit is raised to 512M
33	when the environment allows less. A higher environment limit is kept as is, and `--memory-limit=1G` or
34	`--memory-limit=-1` overrides both.
35	
36	## Parallel Generation
37	
38	Both expensive phases run in worker processes: the sources are parsed in parallel, and the symbol and source pages
39	are rendered in parallel. The workers are forked after the project has been analyzed, so they inherit the documented
40	model instead of being handed a copy of it.
41	
42	The worker count comes from the machine unless a run says otherwise: one worker per logical CPU core, minus one for
43	the process that waits for them, and never more than 16. `--jobs=N` sets the count directly, which is what a CI job
44	sharing its cores with other jobs wants, and `--jobs=1` keeps everything in one process.
45	
46	```bash
47	vendor/bin/doc-gen --jobs=4    # four workers
48	vendor/bin/doc-gen --jobs=1    # one process, no workers
49	```
50	
51	Workers need the `pcntl` extension, and they are not used while OPcache or the JIT is on for the CLI, because their
52	shared memory is not safe to fill from several forked processes at once. A run without them is sequential rather than
53	failed, and the generated site is byte for byte the same however many workers wrote it: the work is split into
54	consecutive jobs and the results are merged in job order, so nothing about the site depends on which worker finished
55	first.
56	
57	## Incremental Generation
58	
59	A run remembers two things in its cache directory: what every source file parsed into, and what every page of the
60	site was written from. The next run parses only the files that changed, and rewrites only the pages that changed.
61	
62	```bash
63	vendor/bin/doc-gen                       # parse and write only what changed
64	vendor/bin/doc-gen --no-cache            # parse everything, write everything, remember nothing
65	vendor/bin/doc-gen --clear-cache         # start from an empty cache
66	vendor/bin/doc-gen --cache-dir=.docgen   # keep the cache somewhere else
67	```
68	
69	Every run reports what it reused:
70	
71	```
72	Generated 1411 pages for 1 packages into build/docs
73	Cache: 861 of 862 sources and 1365 of 1411 pages reused
74	```
75	
76	**The site never depends on the cache.** A cached run writes exactly the site a `--no-cache` run writes, down to the
77	byte, or it writes the page again. That holds because of what the two halves are keyed on:
78	
79	- A **source** is remembered under the content of the file, the package it belongs to, its path in the project, and
80	  the generator itself. Parsing one file reads nothing but that file, so a file that agrees on all four parses into
81	  the same symbols and references it did before.
82	- A **page** is remembered under a digest of everything it is rendered from: the symbol it documents, the relations,
83	  call sites, test cases, and coverage the rest of the project has for it, the navigation of its scope, and what
84	  every name it prints currently resolves to. The last part is what a digest of the page's own data would miss: a
85	  page changes when a class it merely names appears, disappears, or moves, because that is when its links change.
86	  A page is also rewritten when the file it was written to is gone or no longer has the size this cache wrote it
87	  with, so an emptied or half-copied output directory is rebuilt rather than declared up to date.
88	
89	A page the project no longer has is removed from the output directory, so a cached run leaves no page behind that a
90	full run would not have written.
91	
92	The cache is invalidated as a whole by the installed version of the generator — this toolkit and the parser
93	libraries it reads with, each with the exact revision composer installed — so upgrading any of them never serves
94	pages the previous version wrote. A generator changed without being installed again, such as a checkout of the
95	toolkit being worked on or a patched vendor directory, keeps its version and therefore its cache: generate with
96	`--no-cache` while changing the generator itself, or `--clear-cache` once afterwards.
97	
98	Both halves survive branch switching: entries are keyed by content, not by path, and an entry no run has read for a
99	week is dropped. In a comparison run (`--diff`) the sources of both revisions are cached the same way, and the pages
100	are reused when the same two revisions are compared again.
101	
102	The cache directory is a build artifact: ignore it in git, and restore it in CI (for example with `actions/cache`
103	keyed on `composer.lock`) to keep documentation jobs to the size of the change. It holds one entry per source file,
104	of the same order of size as the symbols that file declares, so a project of a thousand files keeps a few tens of
105	megabytes.
106	
107	## Configuration
108	
109	```yaml
110	packages:
111	  - '.'
112	  - 'packages/*'
113	
114	vendor: []
115	
116	vendor_dev: []
117	
118	exclude:
119	  - 'tests/Fixture/*'
120	
121	output: build/docs
122	
123	cache: build/doc-gen-cache
124	
125	title: null
126	deptrac: null
127	coverage: null
128	base_url: null
129	```
130	
131	`packages` (default `['.', 'packages/*']`) lists directory globs, relative to the config file, that are probed for a
132	`composer.json`. This is the only scope control: the documented unit is the composer package, and its PSR-4 autoload
133	map decides which sources are read (`autoload` as API pages, `autoload-dev` as linkable source pages). A repository
134	without a root `composer.json` works because glob entries without a manifest are skipped.
135	
136	`vendor` (default `[]`) and `vendor_dev` (default `[]`) list **composer package name** globs such as `k-kinzal/*` or
137	`*`; matching packages installed under any discovered `vendor/` directory are documented alongside the project
138	packages. `vendor` selects runtime dependencies and `vendor_dev` selects dev dependencies, because the dev tree is
139	usually noise: documenting it is opt-in per glob. The split is read from `composer.lock` when one exists, and derived
140	from the transitive closure of `require` otherwise.
141	
142	Directory names such as `vendor` match nothing, so every glob that documents no installed package of that kind is
143	reported as a warning, as is every selected package that ships no autoloadable source (a phar-only package such as
144	`phpstan/phpstan` can never be documented or linked).
145	
146	`exclude` (default `[]`) lists path globs, relative to the project root, pruned from source scanning.
147	
148	`output` (default `build/docs`) is the site output directory. `title` (default: the root package name, else the
149	project directory name) overrides the site title.
150	
151	`cache` (default `build/doc-gen-cache`) is the directory the parsed sources and the written pages are remembered in;
152	`cache: false` turns caching off for every run of the project, as `--no-cache` does for one run. Keep it outside the
153	output directory: everything below `output` is part of the published site.
154	
155	`deptrac` (default: `deptrac.yaml` at the project root when present) points at a deptrac configuration whose layers
156	and ruleset are rendered as an architecture graph and per-class layer badges. `coverage` (default: none) points at a
157	PHPUnit `--coverage-xml` report directory; when set, every method shows the test cases covering it.
158	
159	`base_url` (default: none) is the absolute address the site is published at, such as
160	`https://example.github.io/project`, without a trailing slash. It is the one thing a site of relative links cannot
161	work out for itself, and it is what the social preview below is rendered from. An address that is not an absolute
162	`http` or `https` URL is rejected.
163	
164	Unknown top-level keys in `doc.yaml` are rejected with an error.
165	
166	## Scope Semantics
167	
168	The documented scope is exactly the union of the discovered packages' PSR-4 autoload directories. Production
169	autoload sources get full API pages, search entries, and navigation; `autoload-dev` sources (tests) get highlighted
170	source pages only, so coverage references and test call sites remain linkable without polluting the API surface.
171	Symbols reachable through more than one package autoload map are documented once, first package wins.
172	
173	## Analysis
174	
175	Types merge the native declaration with PHPDoc, where PHPStan-prefixed tags win over Psalm-prefixed tags, which win
176	over standard tags — generics, array shapes, conditional types, `@template` bounds, and `@phpstan-type` aliases are
177	rendered in full with every documented class name linked. Relations are indexed project-wide: interface implementors,
178	subclasses, trait users, and reference sites (`new`, static and resolvable instance calls, `instanceof`, attributes,
179	type declarations), with call sites listed per method and test references labeled. Examples use the doctest-php
180	notation: `@example` blocks and ` ```php ` fences are rendered as runnable doctest figures with their `// =>`,
181	`// Output:`, and `// throws` assertions styled; single-line `@example expr // note` tags render as display-only
182	examples.
183	
184	## Navigation
185	
186	The site drills down the way rustdoc does. `index.html` lists the packages and their dependency graph; a package page
187	lists its architecture layers, its namespaces with item counts per kind, its documents, and its README; `all-items.html`
188	lists every symbol of the package grouped by kind; a layer page lists the namespaces the layer spans and then its
189	symbols; a namespace page lists its child namespaces and its symbols; a symbol page documents one class, interface,
190	trait, enum, or function.
191	
192	The sidebar is scoped to the current page rather than to the whole project: the sections of the page itself, then the
193	widest scope first — the package entry points with its layers and documents — and then the current namespace with the
194	symbols next to this page, grouped by kind with interfaces first.
195	
196	## Documents
197	
198	Every Markdown file of the repository is rendered as a page under `<package>/doc/`, titled by its first heading, and
199	listed on the package page. Dependency, build, and hidden directories are pruned, and the configured `exclude` globs
200	apply, so the documents are exactly the prose of the analyzed repository. Markdown links between those files resolve
201	to the rendered pages, which makes a `docs/` tree readable inside the site instead of ending in dead relative paths;
202	a link to anything else is rendered as plain text with the target kept as a tooltip.
203	
204	## Symbol pages
205	
206	A symbol page reads from the symbol outwards: first what it is (signature with fully linked types, prose, examples),
207	then its members, then its private surface, and only then what surrounds it — the test cases that exercise it and the
208	relations that connect it.
209	
210	Each member documents its parameters, its return, and its throws as separate labeled blocks, and lists both directions
211	of the dependency question: what calls it, and what it calls. Test call sites never appear there; what tests guarantee
212	is the test case section, which merges the coverage report with the calls made by the analyzed test sources and splits
213	the result into the symbol's own dedicated test class and the other tests that reach it.
214	
215	Relations are grouped by what each reference does — implemented by, extended by, instantiated in, static calls, type
216	declarations, and so on — with every group rendered the same way.
217	
218	## Output
219	
220	The site is fully static and self-contained: relative links only, bundled CSS/JS, client-side search, light and dark
221	themes, and a `.nojekyll` marker, so publishing the output directory with GitHub Pages needs no further setup. The
222	top level contains `index.html`, one directory per package (with its `doc/` documents), `src/` (highlighted sources
223	with line anchors), and `assets/`.
224	
225	## Social Preview
226	
227	A link to a page shared in a chat or on a timeline is rendered as a card by whoever receives it, from tags the page
228	has to carry. Those tags name absolute addresses, so they are written only when `base_url` says where the site is
229	published; without it nothing changes about the site.
230	
231	With it, every page carries its canonical link, a `description` read from what the page documents, and the Open
232	Graph and Twitter tags a card is built from: `og:type`, `og:site_name`, `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:url`, and
233	the image below. The description is the page's own — the summary line of a class, interface, trait, enum, or
234	function, what a package says about itself in its manifest, or what a namespace, layer, document, or source file is
235	— cut to 200 characters.
236	
237	The card image is drawn per site rather than shipped with the generator, so every project previews as itself: a
238	1200×630 PNG at `assets/og-image.png`, in the palette of the site, with the site title, the description of the
239	documented project, and the color band of the generator across the top. Drawing it needs the `gd` extension
240	with FreeType support; without it the run writes no image, the pages carry no `og:image`, the card degrades to a
241	`summary` card, and a warning says so — a card that names an image the site does not serve would be worse.
242	
243	```bash
244	vendor/bin/doc-gen --base-url=https://example.github.io/project
245	```
246	
247	overrides the configured address for one run, which is what a pull request preview published under its own
248	directory wants.
249	
250	## Publishing
251	
252	The site is published by committing the output directory to a branch GitHub Pages serves. Two workflow templates
253	ship with the `/setup-toolkit-doc-gen` skill, in
254	`vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-doc-gen/`:
255	
256	| Template | Trigger | What it does |
257	|----------|---------|--------------|
258	| `docs.yml` | push to the default branch | Generates the site and syncs it to the root of `gh-pages`, keeping `pr/` and `CNAME` |
259	| `docs-preview.yml` | pull request opened, updated, reopened, or closed | Generates the site in diff mode against the base commit into `pr/<number>/`, comments the link on the pull request, and removes the directory when the pull request closes |
260	
261	Both check the documentation branch out with a second `actions/checkout`, sync into it with one `rsync --checksum
262	--delete`, and commit only when the sync changed something. `docs.yml` owns the root of the branch and
263	`docs-preview.yml` owns `pr/<number>/`, so the two never overwrite each other; installing the preview workflow alone
264	would leave the root of the branch empty.
265	
266	The branch and the Pages source are one-time manual setup, because a workflow cannot enable Pages for a repository:
267	
268	```bash
269	git switch --orphan gh-pages
270	git commit --allow-empty -m 'docs: create the documentation branch'
271	git push -u origin gh-pages
272	git switch main
273	```
274	
275	Then set Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source to "Deploy from a branch", branch `gh-pages`, folder
276	`/ (root)`. The site is served at `https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/` and previews at
277	`https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/pr/<number>/`.
278	
279	Pull requests from forks are skipped by the preview workflow: their token is read-only, so it can neither write to
280	the branch nor comment. Publishing those safely needs the `workflow_run` pattern — build on `pull_request` and
281	upload an artifact, publish it from a workflow that runs on the default branch — and never `pull_request_target`,
282	which would run the pull request's code with a write token.
283	
284	This repository runs `docs.yml` (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) and keeps `docs-preview.yml` as a template only,
285	because it is developed on `main` without pull requests.
286	
287	## Local Preview
288	
289	```bash
290	vendor/bin/doc-gen --serve
291	```
292	
293	generates the site and serves it with the PHP built-in web server at `127.0.0.1:8090` until interrupted. Pass
294	`--serve=PORT` or `--serve=HOST:PORT` to change the address.
295	
296	## Diff Mode
297	
298	```bash
299	vendor/bin/doc-gen --diff=main            # main against the working tree
300	vendor/bin/doc-gen --diff=v1.0.0..HEAD    # two revisions
301	vendor/bin/doc-gen --base=main --serve    # the same, previewed locally
302	```
303	
304	`--diff=BASE` compares the working tree against `BASE`; `--diff=BASE..HEAD` compares two revisions. `--base` and
305	`--head` set the same two revisions separately, and `--head` without `--base` is rejected. Diff mode needs the project
306	to live in a git working tree: the base revision — and the head revision when one is named — is checked out into a
307	temporary worktree, the installed dependencies of the project are linked into it so a dependency is not read as newly
308	added, and both checkouts are removed again whatever the run does.
309	
310	Both revisions are analyzed and merged into one site: what the head revision has, plus what the base revision had and
311	the head dropped. Every element carries the state it is in — added, removed, modified, or unchanged — and pages show
312	it down to the single argument of a declaration: a constructor that gained a parameter is shown whole, with only that
313	parameter marked. Symbols are matched by name rather than by position, so moving a method inside a class is not a
314	change; a documentation comment that was only reflowed is not a change either, while its wording is.
315	
316	Removals keep their page. A class the head revision no longer has is documented from the base revision, marked as
317	removed, and its source page is rendered from the base checkout, so the source a removed symbol links to stays
318	readable. Source pages merge both revisions line by line, numbered after the head revision so every `#L…` link of the
319	site keeps working; documents are merged block by block, so a changed paragraph, list, table, or example is marked on
320	its own.
321	
322	Marks use the three state hues and nothing else: **green** for what the head revision added, **red** for what it
323	dropped, **amber** for what it changed. A container carries the state of its parts, so a section, a namespace, an
324	architecture layer, or a package is added only when everything in it is, changed as soon as one part of it is, and
325	unchanged only when nothing in it moved.
326	
327	The generated site serves three display modes, switched next to the theme toggle and remembered across pages:
328	
329	| Mode | Shows |
330	|------|-------|
331	| **Off** | The documentation of the head revision, without any diff marks |
332	| **Diff** | Every page with its additions, removals, and changes marked |
333	| **Changes** | Only what the comparison touched; a page nothing touched says so |
334	
335	Changes mode narrows the navigation with the page: the sidebar keeps the sections, namespaces, layers, and sibling
336	symbols a revision touched and drops the rest, so the way to a change is as short as the change is visible.
337	
338	The mode is applied before the page is laid out, so a page never flashes the wrong colors or the whole file when the
339	changes alone were asked for. Source lines and the arguments of a signature keep their neighbours in Changes mode,
340	because a line or an argument cannot be read without the declaration around it.
341	
342	A coverage report describes the working tree, so it is only read for the head revision; the base revision is analyzed
343	without one, and its methods carry no coverage figure.

# php-ai-toolkit

[![docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-php--ai--toolkit-0969da?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://k-kinzal.github.io/php-ai-toolkit/)

A PHPStan extension that detects anti-patterns commonly introduced by AI code generation, plus output formatters optimized for both AI agents and humans.

## Requirements

- PHP ^8.0
- PHPStan ^1.12 || ^2.0
- PHPUnit ^9.6 || ^10.5 || ^11 || ^12 || ^13

The PHPUnit test reporter supports PHPUnit 9.6 and 10.5 or later through
version-specific adapters. PHPUnit 10+ uses the event extension API, while
PHPUnit 9.6 uses the legacy listener API.

## Quick Start

### 1. Install

This package is not published on Packagist. Install it from the VCS repository by adding the repository to your `composer.json`:

```json
{
    "repositories": [
        {
            "type": "vcs",
            "url": "https://github.com/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit.git"
        }
    ]
}
```

Then require it as a dev dependency:

```bash
composer require --dev k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit
```

### 2. Install AI Agent Skills

```bash
vendor/bin/php-ai-toolkit install
```

Auto-detects AI agent directories (`.claude`, `.agents`, `.continue`, etc.) in your project root and installs skills. Use `--force` to overwrite, `--copy` to copy instead of symlinking.

### 3. Run setup skills

Run the following skills in your AI agent:

- `/setup-toolkit-phpstan` — PHPStan at level max with strict rules and AI error formatter
- `/setup-toolkit-phpunit` — PHPUnit with strict configuration and AI test reporter
- `/setup-toolkit-php-cs-fixer` — PHP-CS-Fixer configuration
- `/setup-toolkit-loc-guard` — LocGuard metrics checks for production source complexity and length limits
- `/setup-toolkit-tree-guard` — TreeGuard directory and file structure constraints
- `/setup-toolkit-doc-gen` — DocGen static documentation site with full types, relations, layers, doctest examples, and a two-revision diff mode
- `/setup-toolkit-deptrac` — Deptrac architecture dependency rules for web apps, CLI apps, libraries, and modular projects

## Template

Read the template from `vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-doc-gen/doc.yaml` and apply it to the

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---------|---------|---------|
| `packages` | `['.', 'packages/*']` | Directory globs probed for a `composer.json`; each hit becomes a documented package. |
| `vendor` | `[]` | Composer package-name globs (`acme/*`, not directory names) of installed **runtime** dependencies to document alongside the project. |
| `vendor_dev` | `[]` | The same for installed **dev** dependencies; keep it empty unless the test tooling itself needs documenting. |
| `exclude` | `[]` | Path globs, relative to the project root, pruned from source scanning. |

The optional keys `title`, `deptrac`, and `coverage` override the site title, the deptrac config used for the
architecture layer graph (auto-detected at `deptrac.yaml`), and the PHPUnit `--coverage-xml` report directory used

The documented unit is the composer package: production autoload sources become API pages while `autoload-dev`

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace PhpAiToolkit\DocGen\Config;

use function is_string;

use PhpAiToolkit\DocGen\DocGenException;

use function preg_match;
use function rtrim;
use function sprintf;
use function trim;

/**
 * Normalizes the address of the repository a documented project lives in.
 *
 * A generated site is the read side of a repository, and a reader who found
 * an answer in it usually wants the code that answer was read from, so the
 * site names where that code lives. Only an absolute http address can be
 * linked to from a page: a value that is not one is rejected where a project
 * configured it, and ignored where it merely stands in a manifest that is
 * read for other reasons.
 */
final class RepositoryUrl
{
    /**
     * Returns one repository address, or null when there is none to link to.
     *
     * Anything that is not an absolute http address is no address at all
     * here, because a page can only link to what a browser can follow.
     */
    public function read(mixed $value): ?string
    {
        if (!is_string($value)) {
            return null;
        }

            return null;

     * Returns one configured address without its trailing slash.
     *
     * An empty value is the same answer as no value at all: the site names
     * no repository, rather than one that resolves nowhere.
     *
     * @throws DocGenException when the value is not an absolute http address
     */
    public function normalize(?string $value): ?string
    {
        if ($value === null || trim($value) === '') {
            return null;
        }

        $url = $this->read($value);
        if ($url === null) {
            throw new DocGenException(sprintf(

        }

    /**

    {

    }

    /**

    }

        (new RepositoryUrl())->normalize('git@github.com:example/project.git');
    }
}

## Back to the Repository

A generated site is the read side of a repository, so every page carries the way back to it: the page shell links the
host of the repository next to the theme toggle, and a package page names it in full as its `Repository` row.

The address is read from the `composer.json` of the package itself — `support.source` first, because that is what
composer links a package to its code with, and `homepage` after it, because it is the only address a package that
declares no source offers a reader. Only an absolute `http` or `https` address is linked, so a `git@…` or `git://`
source is ignored rather than rendered as a link a browser cannot follow. `repository` in `doc.yaml` overrides what
the project's own packages declare; a documented dependency always links to what its own manifest says, because it is
published from somewhere else. A package that says nothing gets no link rather than a guess.

The other direction is the repository's own: the site is published at one address, so a link to it from the README,
from `homepage`, or from `support.docs` in `composer.json` closes the loop.

Forbid expecting the exceptions that mean the code is broken

A test that writes expectException(LogicException::class) asserts that
broken code fails. That is true of every program, so the case proves
nothing about the class under test and belongs deleted rather than
fixed. NoBrokenCodeExpectationRule reports it, and says so.

The taxonomy is the one ForbidBroadCatchRule already keeps out of catch
blocks: the LogicException family is a programmer error, the Error
family is an engine failure, and expectException is a catch in disguise,
so what may not be handled may not be expected either. Throwable joins
them for a different reason — it matches every failure at once, so a
passing expectation cannot tell the failure the test meant to trigger
from a typo in the test itself. The RuntimeException family stays
testable, because those are the failures a caller is expected to handle,
and the root Exception is left alone so that a documented contract
extending it can still be expected.

Both expectException() and expectExceptionObject() are checked, whether
called through $this, self, static, or parent, and only where the
expected type is statically known: a dynamic class-string argument or an
object without a single known class is not reported. The rule applies
across the Tests\ namespace, since the construct exists nowhere else.

Evidence, Outcome, and Probe name what an agent was doing — collecting
